$comment: Worked example (issue #7): a filled migration-state.json for the fictional project 'duplifind', snapshot mid-Stage 7 of an L3 autopilot run (issue #22), deliberately showing one unit in each of the six statuses. Validates against migration-state.schema.json (CI: framework/state/check_examples.py) and passes the coherence checks of tools/state.py validate. Walkthrough: README.md next to this file.

project.name: duplifind
project.workload: nightly near-duplicate sweep over the 10k-doc corpus (1.4 GB)

invariants: Invariant: tokens are lowercased, NFC-normalized, split on whitespace
Invariant: empty input raises ValueError (never returns [])
Postcondition: duplicates and input order are preserved — dedupe is a separate unit

units.notes: First unit ported (Stage 4, candidate c2; c1 missed NFC normalization, 2/250 divergent). Stable in Rust since 2026-06-18; Python fallback retired 2026-10-15 after the agreed two-quarter stability window (Stage 7 step 4) — the rust side is now the only side. The Stage-2 judge-first demo for this unit is preserved in oracle/u-tokenize-1.verdict.json.

sessions.name: unit-u-tokenize-1-reviewer-r1
sessions.outcome: APPROVE (fresh-input oracle rerun + attribution diff clean)

invariants: Invariant: output preserves input order of first occurrences

units.notes: BTreeSet replaces the CPython dict used as an ordered set; first-occurrence order carried by an index vector, so dict-ordering risk never materialized. Oracle equivalent 240/240 on the first candidate. Python fallback still live (Stage 7 retires it deliberately, unit by unit).

contract.type_signature: duplifind.shingle.shingles(tokens: list[str], k: int, weights: dict[str, float]) -> list[tuple[int, float]]
invariants: Invariant: shingles are k-grams hashed to u64 (Stage-1 redesign)
Invariant: non-finite weights are rejected (human ruling 2026-07-21)

parity.divergence_note: Corpus run i=137 feeds a NaN shingle weight: the Python reference propagates it into a NaN-poisoned score, the Rust candidate raises ValueError (int/float semantics were not the issue; error-vs-value is). Human ruling 2026-07-21: rejecting non-finite weights is the contract going forward — reference updated after cutover planning, release note written. Divergence recorded, never normalized away.

units.notes: Ships with one explained divergence (209/210 exact) — the Volatility3 pattern: exact parity everywhere except where a written, human-ruled explanation exists. Oracle verdict stays 'divergent' honestly; the explanation is the deliverable, not a silenced judge. Python fallback live.

sessions.name: unit-u-shingle-3-reviewer-r1
sessions.outcome: ESCALATE the divergence; human ruled it acceptable -> APPROVE with note

invariants: Invariant: serialized bloom-filter bytes are a deterministic function of inserted docs
Invariant: queries never observe partial inserts

parity.divergence_note: 19/180 corpus runs serialize the bloom filter with different bytes: FxHashMap iteration order leaks into the byte stream where the reference emits CPython dict insertion order. Query-level parity is 180/180 — the divergence is serialization-only. Minimal repro: escalations/u-index-4.md.

units.notes: Budget exhausted at round 5 (MAX_ROUNDS hit twice — mandatory escalation). Fix requires a deterministic serializer over a BTreeMap: a data-structure redesign, which is a Stage-1-semantics proposal needing human sign-off, never improvised mid-loop. Python fallback is the live side for this unit.

sessions.name: unit-u-index-4-reviewer-r1
sessions.outcome: ESCALATE — redesign required, out of unit scope

units.notes: The Rust port passed every correctness gate (oracle 120/120 equivalent, miri + clippy green), but the Stage-5 matched-corpus benchmark showed the numpy-vectorized Python side matches it within overlapping confidence intervals (bench verdict + repro corpus committed). Human decision 2026-09-30: keep Python as the live side — 'optimized Python matches the port' is the documented no-win outcome, and keeping Python is a success, not a failure (MIGRATION_PROMPT.md failure-mode table). Rust candidate stays behind the per-unit fallback switch for revisit.

invariants: Invariant: vector length fixed by config.featurize.dim

units.notes: Added 2026-10-24 via an approved scope_change (upstream feature request duplifind#331, surfaced by the Stage-7 upstream watcher). Contract extraction is queued; translation has not started. Units can legitimately be pending during Stage 7 — maintenance mode re-opens the backlog, it does not freeze it.

human_gates.note: Stage 0: go — 58% projected end-to-end saving on the nightly sweep; I/O share 11% (under the no-go bar)
Stage 1: k-gram shingles hashed to u64 (dict-of-dicts -> typed struct)
Stage 6: clean shadow window 2026-09-05..09-08 (0 divergent / 0.4M sampled requests); rollback pin kept in the release notes
evidence: rollback_tested=true (deploys the old pin, verifies, returns)

human_gates.note: u-index-4 divergent after 5 rounds (bloom-filter bytes); repro + BTreeMap serializer redesign proposal in escalations/u-index-4.md
evidence: deferred=drains into the end-of-run escalation dossier

human_gates.note: 2026-10-24: add duplifind.featurize to scope (upstream #331) — the 'any scope change later' mandatory gate
evidence: override=operator approved out-of-band (policy SC-1 default is reject; a human may still decide any gate at any level)
